title: pkix-difftest: pin x509-limbo as a submodule so Dependabot watches it
description:
The x509-limbo corpus is a Tier-2 corpus in diff-harness.yml, and that workflow records that the limbo testdata is not in this repo and needs a scrape/clone step. An unpinned clone means the corpus the harness compares against is whatever upstream HEAD is on the day CI runs, so a baseline measured one week is not the baseline the next -- and a changed case count arrives as a surprise rather than a decision.

x509-limbo is a GitHub repository, so GitHub can do the watching rather than us:

  - add it as a git submodule, pinned to a commit
  - .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem: gitsubmodule

Dependabot then opens a pull request when upstream moves. That is strictly better than a cron job comparing digests: the diff is reviewable, the full diff-harness runs on the PR, and the new case count arrives with CI's verdict attached.

Replaces the scrape/clone step rather than adding to it.

Decide before implementing:

1. Submodule vs. vendoring the corpus outright. A submodule keeps the repo small and the provenance exact, but every clone needs --recursive and CI needs submodules: true. Vendoring makes the tree self-contained and offline, which matches how PKITS is handled here, at the cost of size and a manual refresh.
2. Whether a Dependabot PR that changes the corpus should be allowed to fail the harness. It usually should: that failure is the signal. But it means a red PR nobody opened, which is the thing external-anchors.yml deliberately keeps out of quality-gates.yml.

Not urgent. It is a correctness-of-measurement issue, not a defect in pkix-path: nothing is scored wrongly today, the baseline is just not reproducible across time.

Related: PKITS needs none of this. NIST's page confirms PKITS 1.0.1 was posted 14 April 2011 and nothing newer exists, NIST is not on GitHub, csrc.nist.gov has no stable digest endpoint, and our copy derives from golang/go's testdata subtree, which Dependabot cannot watch at subpath granularity.
close_reason:
Done in e445a035.

Chose the submodule over vendoring: the corpus is 74MB and limbo.json alone is 41MB, and a submodule is not fetched unless asked for, so an ordinary clone is unaffected. Pinned at b12423782a88abead01141fa6582254e3eb49e74. x509-limbo turned out to be its own cargo workspace, so the root manifest needs no exclude -- the concern in the bead about a nested Cargo.toml did not materialise.

On the second decision in this bead -- whether a corpus PR may fail the harness -- yes, deliberately, and the dependabot.yml comments say why: that failure is the signal, and the reviewer decides whether a moved count is upstream adding cases or pkix-path regressing. Kept out of quality-gates.yml by being a Dependabot PR rather than a push-path job, which is the separation external-anchors.yml already established.

Correction to this bead's framing: there was no scrape/clone step to replace. diff-harness.yml considered one and rejected it as CI flake surface, so limbo was never fetched in CI at all -- the Limbo subcommand documented ~/GIT/x509-limbo/limbo.json, a developer's own clone. The manifest argument now defaults to the submodule.

Pinning immediately found drift in both directions, which is the whole argument for it:

1. The pinned commit has 9807 testcases against baseline-limbo.json's 9726, so the baseline was already measuring a different corpus than anyone would reproduce today.
2. corpus::limbo::Feature is exhaustive on purpose, and upstream has since added has-mldsa -- which made all 9807 testcases fail to deserialize over six of them. Fixed in the same commit, because pinning at a commit whose manifest does not load would be a broken intermediate state. Nothing here verifies ML-DSA so dropping those six is correct.

A pkix-path-only run over the pinned corpus loads and classifies 9731 in-scope testcases with 2895 ground-truth disagreements, against the baseline's 9726 and 2902. The class counts from that run are not comparable to the baseline: with one oracle there is nothing to diverge from, so everything classifies as Agreement. Baselines deliberately left alone -- they were taken with all three oracles and re-taking them needs the pyca sidecar and a ~14 minute run, so re-baselining belongs to whoever next moves the pin.
